key_insight: Routine clinical data collected during tuberculosis treatment predicts end-of-therapy status reasonably well, but it only modestly predicts later relapse and loses value after about month 3.
clinical_relevance: For trial readouts and follow-up planning, post-baseline clinical variables can improve relapse risk stratification, but they are not strong enough to replace relapse-specific biomarkers.
method: Harmonized data from 2 Phase 3 TB trials (2,918 participants)
Built time-resolved prediction models at monthly intervals from baseline to therapy end
Compared tabular features with large language model-derived embeddings and longitudinal models
evidence_signal: End-of-therapy outcome prediction improved after month 3 with ROC-AUC up to 0.84, while relapse prediction stayed modest (ROC-AUC 0.58–0.63) and then declined; embeddings matched tabular relapse performance and sometimes improved end-of-therapy prediction.
watch_item: These models use routine clinical variables and may be less interpretable or transferable across settings, so they should not be used as stand-alone relapse predictors without external validation.
paper_title: Time-resolved predictability of end-of-therapy outcome and relapse after cure in Phase 3 tuberculosis trials
